description.p: Rustab is a modern, native Linux desktop GUI for viewing, editing, adding, and removing entries in /etc/fstab, built with stability and data safety as the top priority.
Rustab combines a clean, intuitive interface with a safety-first architecture:

ul.li: Full fstab syntax support: UUIDs, LABELs, device paths, network sources, bind mounts, swap entries, and systemd-generator options (x-systemd.*), with comments and formatting round-tripping perfectly
Atomic writes and automatic timestamped backups on every save, with mandatory findmnt --verify validation before anything is written to disk
A clear real-vs-sandbox target indicator and a mandatory diff review before saving, so every change is visible and reviewed before it persists
Device and mount-point pickers to make entry creation easier, with graceful fallback to manual entry if the underlying system tools are unavailable
A dev sandbox by default - pointing the app at the real /etc/fstab is an explicit, auditable choice, never the default

description.p: Editing the real /etc/fstab requires administrator privileges and shows an explicit confirmation step; sandbox edits never require elevation.

description.p: Native aarch64 (ARM64) builds for the .deb, .rpm, and AppImage packages, so Rustab runs on devices like the Raspberry Pi.
